title: Negotiation microscripts & risk summaries
content:
Purpose: quick personal reference for 1) short negotiation lines to use on discovery calls and redline passes, 2) rapid-risk taxonomy to prioritize clauses, 3) fallback language and escalation triggers. Mostly bullety, meant for fast copy-paste into RFCs or Slack to ops/eng.

Microscripts (1-2 sentence lines to use live):
- "We can accept reasonable data export requests if we get a scoped notice period and a minimal export fee to cover retrieval—can we agree on 30 days and a defined S3 delivery?"
- "For indemnity, we can agree to direct damages capped to the fees paid in the prior 12 months; broad third-party IP indemnity is negotiable if you accept a mutual carve-out for model outputs and a notice-and-control right."
- "We want availability SLAs tied to a credits refund; for anything below 99.5% we propose a tiered credit schedule rather than unlimited liability—does that work?"
- "We need to treat model weights and training artifacts as Redwood property; we can discuss embeddings/outputs as customer data with usage restrictions."
- "On subprocessors: we use cloud vendors and managed inference partners. We can provide a list and offer 30-day notice before adding new ones — is that acceptable?"

Rapid risk taxonomy (priority buckets for quick triage):
- High (must-fix before signature): unlimited liability, uncapped data liability for customer PII, irrevocable ownership transfer of model/weights, break-glass access without audit, permanent data retention clauses.
- Medium (negotiate hard, acceptable with mitigation): broad IP indemnity for model outputs, long export/residency obligations (>90 days), aggressive audit windows that imply shared credentials, SLA penalties that compound to >100% of fees.
- Low (tradeable): 3rd-party subcontractor notice, standard confidentiality terms, short-term warranty language, reasonable escrow for seeds/keys with lawyer-reviewed escrow agent.

Examples of quick-line edits (use in redline):
- Data export: replace "Customer may request export within 6 months" with "Customer may request export within 30 days of termination; Redwood will provide export in a structured format and make commercially reasonable efforts to deliver within 30 days. Fees limited to direct costs."
- Indemnity cap: replace open-ended indemnity with "each party's aggregate liability to the other shall be limited to the amount of fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the twelve months preceding the claim, except for willful misconduct or gross negligence."
- IP ownership: change "Customer owns model outputs" to "Customer owns Customer Data and model outputs derived exclusively from Customer Data; Redwood retains ownership of models, weights, and improvements independent of Customer Data."

Negotiation play (trade vectors to propose when counterparty asks for more):
- Ask for security/compliance concessions in exchange for softened liability (e.g., SOC2 report + quarterly penetration test result).
- If they want no cap on liability for data, propose a smaller cap for data liability with strict behavioral covenants (encryption, access controls) and a carve-out for aggregated/anonymous output.
- Offer a short demo of our VPC/private deployment features as a commercial sweetener for residency demands.
- If they insist on audit rights, require a defined scope, pre-approved auditors, and 30 days' notice with security controls in place.

Escalation triggers (send to GC/Head of Sales/Eng):
- Customer demands language that exposes Redwood to criminal liability or government seizure without process. Escalate immediately.
- Customer wants full ownership/transfer of model artifacts or rights to redistribute our models.
- Audit requests that require on-site access to prod systems or live credentials.
- SLA remedies that convert to injunctive relief or unlimited damages.

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Confirm what our default export format is (parquet, JSONL?) and whether we can standardize a 30-day export SLA as a product feature.
- Check with engineering: how long to reasonably produce bulk training artifacts for a terminated account? Ticket ENG-4521.
- Investigate whether we can automate a subprocessors notification endpoint for customers to subscribe to — reduces negotiation friction.

Common counterparty asks and best responses:
- "We need 24/7 support and a penalty for downtime." -> "We offer enterprise support add-on and can scope a credits-based SLA; for higher availability guarantees we recommend Dedicated capacity with tighter SLOs."
- "We require source code escrow." -> "We can discuss escrow for customer-specific integrations (connectors), but not for our core runtime or model weights. Propose limited-scope escrow instead."
- "We want unrestricted model retraining rights using our data." -> "We can license outputs back to you for your internal use but maintain model IP rights; suggest a limited license for derivative training if mutually agreed with revenue share/terms."

Fallback language bank (quick paste snippets):
- ""Each party's liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the 12 months prior to the claim, or (b) $50,000, except for claims arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence.""
- ""Redwood will list subprocessors and provide 30 days' notice before any material change; customers may terminate certain services if a material unconsented subprocessor is added.""
- ""Customer Data shall mean data provided by Customer to Redwood. Customer retains ownership of Customer Data; Redwood may use aggregated, anonymized telemetry for service improvement.""

Quick escalation script for AE when sign-off needed:
- "Legal, heads-up: customer X asked to remove liability cap for data and wants a 3-year export guarantee. Proposed counter: cap equals 12 months fees; export provision limited to 30 days and fees for retrieval. Need quick sign-off or ask for commercial exception."

One-liners to calm counterparties (tone -> collaborative):
- "We want to make this work — tell me the real business need driving this clause and we'll find a secure, auditable way to meet it."
- "Totally understand the ask; in our experience a short, scoped export window plus a cost recovery fee solves most regulatory needs without operational risk."

References / bookmarks (to check before next call):
- Contract Playbook (link above)
- ENG-4521 (production export runbook)
- SOC2 report (drive: shared_drives/company/compliance/soc2-2024.pdf)

Bottom line: prioritize removal of uncapped liabilities and any clause that effectively transfers ownership of our model IP. Use microscripts to move fast on calls and push complex asks into written, scoped commitments that we can operationalize. Keep this doc minimal and copyable.
